newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips as two leading dlr buyers bid.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips as two leading dlr buyers bid.

text.p: Dollar buying by two major players enlivened the inter-bank dollar-rupee market on Monday with spot rupee slipping by four paise, dealers said.
Spot rupee closed at 35.875/885, down from the opening level of 35.855/865. The rupee saw a high of 35.855 and a low of 35.895 during the day, dealers said.
They said bids by an influential Calcutta-based state-run bank, one of the two leading market players, dragged the rupee.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the other major player in the market, bought dollars on a smaller scale. "RBI must have bought some $50-$70 million today," a dealer said.
RBI bought May and June dollars in outright deals.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed the day at 6.97 percent, down from the weekend close of 7.14 percent.
A slight shortfall in supply also fuelled the dollar's rise on Monday, dealers said.
Some dealers had expected the RBI to reduce its intervention on Monday after the finance minister's weekend statement that market forces should determine the rate.
"In India, the central bank determines the exchange rate, not the market," said the chief dealer at a Bombay bank.
"Or maybe they are the market," he said, in a joking reference to the central bank and the Calcutta-based state-run bank.
